t.E216.agn: In its opinion of 13 July 2004 EFSA set a group ADI of 0–10 mg/kg body weight in total for methyl and ethyl paraben, but did not include propyl paraben in this group. The reason was that propyl paraben had shown effects on sex hormones and male reproductive organs in young rats and that a clear no-effect dose (NOAEL) could not be established; therefore no ADI could be proposed for propyl paraben. Following this, E 216 was removed from the EU list of additives by Directive 2006/52/EC.
t.E216.body: Parabens are well absorbed when taken orally and are rapidly broken down in the body (in the liver and kidneys) to p-hydroxybenzoic acid; the ester form can rarely be measured in the blood. This acid is excreted in urine, either free or bound to glycine and glucuronic acid.
t.E216.eff.0.a: No no-effect dose could be established
t.E216.eff.0.t: Effects on sex hormones and male reproductive organs were seen in young rats; it was therefore removed from the EU list of additives
t.E216.eval: In the EU it was removed from the list of additives by Directive 2006/52/EC (EFSA 2004: no ADI could be proposed because of hormonal and male reproductive system effects in young rats). In the US, California AB 418 bans it in food from 2027.
t.E216.found.0: Not authorised in food in the EU since 2006
t.E216.prod: A paraben produced chemically by esterifying p-hydroxybenzoic acid with n-propanol.
t.E216.regx.0: Propyl paraben was not included in the group ADI; no ADI could be proposed because of hormonal and male reproductive organ effects in young rats.
t.E216.regx.1: Removed from the 95/2/EC list of additives by Directive 2006/52/EC; not included in the list in Annex II Part B of 1333/2008.
t.E216.regx.2: Use in food banned from 1 January 2027 under AB 418 (California Food Safety Act).
t.E216.summary: A synthetic preservative from the paraben group (an ester of p-hydroxybenzoic acid). Used against moulds and yeasts; more common in cosmetics than in food.
t.E216.what: A paraben-type preservative that slows the growth of moulds and yeasts; it is no longer authorised as a food additive in the EU.
